met_analysis:
The Low Pressure area over North Odisha and adjoining Jharkhand & Gangetic West Bengal now lies over Gangetic West Bengal and adjoining Jharkhand & north Odisha at 0830 hrs IST of today, 17th July, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation now extends upto 5.8 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height. It is very likely to weaken gradually during next 24 hrs.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Amritsar, Chandigarh, Shahjahanpur, Basti, Patna, centre of Low Pressure area over Gangetic West Bengal and adjoining Jharkhand & north Odisha and thence southeastwards towards Northeast Bay of Bengal and extends upto 0.9 km above mean sea level.
A fresh Western Disturbance seen as cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan & neighbourhood at 5.8 km above mean sea level with a trough aloft with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level runs roughly along Long. 67°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over north Haryana & neighbourhood persists and now lies at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood & extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
A trough runs from North Lakshadweep area to southwest Bay of Bengal across north Kerala, South Interior Karnataka and north Tamilnadu at 7.6 km above mean sea level.
The trough from the cyclonic circulation associated the Low Pressure area to east-central Arabian Sea between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over Jammu division & neighbourhood between 4.5 & 5.8 km above mean sea level with the trough aloft has moved away northeastwards.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over East Uttar Pradesh & adjoining Bihar and extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
